---
title: "Reproducibility"
---

## Seeds everywhere

Every demo and every executed cell on this site fixes its RNG seed.
`SimulationConfig.seed` and `InferenceConfig.seed` thread a single
generator through observation noise and the particle filter respectively,
so a given configuration is repeatable in the same numerical environment.
Matching seeds alone do not guarantee identical trajectories or final numbers
across platforms: NumPy draws, floating-point arithmetic, BLAS, and the host
math library can differ. The frozen SMC replays therefore compare floating
results with tolerances while checking counts and controls exactly. Use the
locked dependencies and the displayed settings when reproducing a page.

## Tests

The default suite — `uv run pytest` — covers the forward model's physical
domain, public data contracts, all resampling variants, adaptive tempering,
conjugate evidence checks, MH invariance and rejection, observation
atomicity, prior support, contrast-space likelihoods, the public API, wheel
entry points, and visualization. Long-running fixed-seed acceptance scans are
excluded by default (`uv run pytest -m slow` runs them). See
[`tests/`](https://github.com/jbwhit/clocks/tree/main/tests) for the
current inventory; the README deliberately does not quote a test count,
because hardcoded counts go stale.

## CI

Three workflows run on GitHub Actions:

- [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/jbwhit/clocks/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml)
  runs tests and lint on pushes to `main` and on non-draft pull requests
  targeting `main`, including when a draft is marked ready for review.
- [`site.yml`](https://github.com/jbwhit/clocks/blob/main/.github/workflows/site.yml)
  is triggered by each push to `main` and re-renders and redeploys this site, so every
  figure drawn by an executed cell is redrawn at deploy time: most by running
  the model again from source, and the density figure from a committed data
  file. The demo GIFs and the echolocation range-study PNG are the exceptions:
  they are committed images, described in the next section.
- [`site-check.yml`](https://github.com/jbwhit/clocks/blob/main/.github/workflows/site-check.yml)
  renders this site and runs the link and figure checks on non-draft pull
  requests targeting `main` that touch the site or the library, so a broken
  page is caught before it merges.

## Where the figures come from {#sec-figures}

The story pages keep commentary on these figures' origin to a short caveat.
This section summarizes where each came from and what it does and does not
establish. The
[development calibration report](https://github.com/jbwhit/clocks/blob/main/docs/2026-08-16-development-calibration.md)
is the record of the August 2026 release: the generating commit and the hashes
of the files that release shipped, not of every figure now on this site.

**Demo animations.** Each committed GIF is the packaged default output of its
`uv run demo-*` command, generated explicitly from the corrected physics and
SMC implementation after one-shot certification. The commands regenerate their
scenarios, but image encoders are not claimed to be byte-deterministic across
tool versions. Each animation depicts one named finite realization: a fixed
scenario and seed. None establishes a population recovery rate. Where a story
page also runs a smaller example in an executed cell, that is a separate finite
run whose settings are shown in the cell.

**Replay data.** The density figure on
[Beyond Point Masses](../story/beyond-point-masses.qmd) is drawn when the site
is built, from `assets/replays/demo_density.npz`, the recorder's archive of the
demo's packaged run: 60 observations, 2,000 particles and seed 42. The archive
holds the configuration, seed and observations, a summary of the cloud before
any observation and after each, and a 500-particle sample for display. Tests
run the demo again; they compare its inputs, the computed ones (clock
positions, true rates and readings) at `rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12` and the rest
exactly, and its summaries within stated bounds; they do not require the same
random path. `uv run demo-density` records the same configured scenario and
draws its result. The archive is one finite realization: it establishes no
population recovery rate.

The density demo samples a uniform box in $(\mu,\sigma,A)$ conditioned on
that box and weak-field validity, and uses the same support for its prior
density.

**Echolocation animation.** The committed GIF is the packaged default output
from the corrected contrast-space SMC release, not a re-render of the current
code. Its differential-rates panel draws the forward model evaluated at the
posterior mean; the code now plots the posterior mean of the particles' own
predictions, so that panel will change when the assets are next regenerated.
It places the mass at two circumradii along a fixed off-axis direction, and
is one fixed-seed visualization at the closest, most favorable range, not a
reliability measurement.

**Model-comparison runs.** The committed GIF on
[How Many Masses?](../story/how-many-masses.qmd) is the packaged default run:
80 observations, 2,000 particles per candidate, and seed 42. With K=2 truth,
its final estimate is K=2: 0.3990 and K=3: 0.6010. The executed cell on that
page is a separate 25-observation, 400-particle calculation that ends near
K=2: 0.740 and K=3: 0.260. A different finite data horizon changes the
evidence supplied by the noisy realization, and a different finite-particle
budget changes the Monte Carlo estimate of that evidence. The split between
two and three masses also moves substantially with the inference seed at
these budgets, so neither number is a claim about which model generated the
data. Comparing models responsibly means examining data horizon,
particle-count, and seed sensitivity rather than reading one run's extra
decimal places as certainty.

**Echolocation range study.** The range harness behind the figure on the
[echolocation page](../story/gravitational-echolocation.qmd) sweeps the
declared circumradius grid along the same fixed off-axis direction as the
animation, at one fixed mass, and records position error, mass error, posterior
standard deviations, coverage, residuals, SMC controls, and forward-model
evaluation counts. Development seeds 0–11 selected the controls by the
declared ranking
(`uv run scripts/scan_echolocation_range.py --seed-block 0`), and the
controls and acceptance tolerances were frozen before the reserved block was
run. The reserved 400–411 block was then run exactly once for the
corrected implementation, using the scenario-default cell via
`--seed-block 400`; protected blocks reject control overrides.

The displayed study was regenerated directly from the certified block-400
records. The frozen cell passed 46/72 cases overall; pass counts from close to
far were 12, 12, 11, 8, 3, 0. The close range passed 12/12. The far/close
median position-standard-deviation ratio was 66.524, above the frozen factor
20 gate, and the 12/12 far-range three-standard-deviation coverage is retained
as a diagnostic rather than promoted after inspection into a new gate.

The completed protocol guards against tuning directly to the reported holdout,
but its fixed seeds provide regression and calibration evidence only for those
simulated cases. It does not estimate population reliability or justify a
universal pass probability. Any claimed sensing horizon must therefore be
attached to a stated noise model, prior, particle budget, SMC controls, pass
rule, and finite seed set, not promoted to a property of the population.

Taken together: the protected fixed-seed results establish deterministic
regression cases, not a population reliability estimate. SMC evidence is
similarly a
consistent Monte Carlo estimator with finite-particle sampling error, not a
deterministic exact integral.

## Locked Python dependencies

`uv.lock` is committed; CI enforces the Python package resolution with
`--locked` in `ci.yml` and `--frozen` in the site build. The lock covers
package versions for its supported Python-version markers. It does **not** pin
the Python interpreter's patch release; Quarto is pinned separately, in the
site workflows. So the repository does not claim a fully bit-reproducible
rendering toolchain.
